<!--
STATISTICAL TOOLS USED IN THIS FILE
(full definitions in statistical_tools_glossary (Claude).R; this is the subset
that actually appears below)

MODEL FITTING
- lmer() [lme4] -- Gaussian linear mixed model; SENSITIVITY check
  version of most models here (Rule 2), usually on log(Flux).
- glmer() [lme4] -- generalized linear mixed model (distmodel only).
- glmmTMB() [glmmTMB] -- PRIMARY model fitter for this project. Set
  family = Gamma(link = "log") for Flux everywhere it's used here.

SIGNIFICANCE / MODEL COMPARISON
- Anova() [car] -- Type II significance test on a fitted model's fixed
  effects. Capital A; different from anova() below.
- anova() [base/lme4] -- either a fixed-effects table for one model, or
  (with two model arguments) a likelihood ratio test comparing two
  NESTED models, e.g. deposition_model_base vs. deposition_model_slope.
- AIC() -- compares non-nested models by fit-vs-complexity tradeoff
  (lower = better); used for distsitemodel_glmm vs. its dispersion/noGM
  variants.

POST-HOC / EFFECT SIZE
- emmeans() / emtrends() [emmeans] -- model-predicted means (emmeans)
  or slopes (emtrends) for specific factor levels/combinations, with
  pairwise comparisons. type = "response" back-transforms Gamma/log-
  link estimates onto the Flux scale.
- ggpredict() [ggeffects] -- model-predicted values across a range of a
  continuous predictor (z_star here), for plotting a fitted line/ribbon.
- r.squaredGLMM() [MuMIn] -- marginal/conditional R² for a mixed model.

DISTRIBUTION / RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS
- shapiro.test() / qqnorm() / qqline() -- normality check on raw Flux
  (rejects normality -- part of the Gamma justification, Rule 2). Not
  the right diagnostic for a fitted GLMM's residuals -- that's DHARMa.
- simulateResiduals() / plot() / testDispersion() [DHARMa] -- simulation-
  based residual diagnostics appropriate for a Gamma GLMM, where raw
  residuals never look normal even in a well-fit model. See
  statistical_tools_glossary (Claude).R for how the simulation actually works.

VISUALIZATION
- stat_halfeye() [ggdist] -- draws a half-violin/density ("cloud") of
  the raw distribution; used with geom_boxplot()/geom_jitter() to build
  the raincloud plot comparing Flux distribution shape (skewness)
  between Ramped and Scarped, on the raw (not log-transformed) scale.
-->


```{r, working directory and master data file}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = 'C:/Users/savan/OneDrive - San Francisco State University/ProjectData/GitHub/DepositionSFB/data')

master_tier5_byrep <- readr::read_csv("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\master_tier5_byrep.csv")

master_tier5_byrep_clean <- master_tier5_byrep |> 
  filter(Flux > 0, 
         Dist != 48)

# FIX: master_tier5_byrep.csv doesn't carry step1's factor level order (CSVs
# only store text, not R's factor metadata) -- without setting this
# explicitly, R/glmmTMB default to alphabetical order, which makes
# Ramped (not Scarped) the reference level, silently flipping every
# model's baseline from what step1 intended. Matches the level order
# set in step1_master_analysis_cleanup.Rmd.
master_tier5_byrep_clean <- master_tier5_byrep_clean %>%
  mutate(marsh_edge_type = factor(marsh_edge_type, levels = c("Scarped", "Ramped")))

month_levels <- c("Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec",
                   "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun")

master_tier5_byrep <- master_tier5_byrep %>%
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = month_levels))

master_tier5_byrep_clean <- master_tier5_byrep_clean %>%
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = month_levels))

# ADDED: averaged companion, same filter/factor steps as master_tier5_byrep
# above, applied to master_tier5.csv (the averaged tier) instead.
master_tier5 <- readr::read_csv("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\master_tier5.csv")

master_tier5_clean <- master_tier5 |> 
  filter(Flux > 0, 
         Dist != 48)

master_tier5_clean <- master_tier5_clean %>%
  mutate(marsh_edge_type = factor(marsh_edge_type, levels = c("Scarped", "Ramped")))

master_tier5 <- master_tier5 %>%
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = month_levels))

master_tier5_clean <- master_tier5_clean %>%
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = month_levels))
```

```{r, ADDED consolidated averaged-side data prep}
# This file mutates master_tier5_byrep_clean incrementally throughout
# (Site releveling, Tran/Study.Phase factor conversions, a Flux>0/
# finite-log safety filter before transite1, etc.), scattered across
# many chunks -- several inside plot-only chunks not duplicated here
# (see the note at the end of this file for what wasn't ported).
#
# Rather than replicate every scattered mutation in lockstep, the
# consequential ones (the ones that matter for model FITTING, not just
# plot cosmetics/ordering) are consolidated here, once, applied to
# master_tier5_clean up front. Cosmetic factor-level reordering used
# only by skipped plots (e.g. Site level order for x-axis display) is
# NOT replicated here since it doesn't change model results.
#
# IMPORTANT: the byrep side REBUILDS master_tier5_byrep_clean partway
# through the file (originally ~line 812) as `filter(Flux > 0)` only --
# dropping the initial Dist != 48 filter. That rebuilt version (Flux>0,
# Dist=48 INCLUDED) is what most models downstream of that point
# actually use (the z* models, transite1, marsh_edge_model*,
# marsh_group_model, deposition_model*) -- only avgdist and models built
# from it re-exclude Dist=48 on top of that. Matching that here:

master_tier5_clean <- master_tier5 |>
  filter(Flux > 0)   # matches the byrep-side rebuild; Dist=48 included

# Matches the Flux>0 / finite-log safety filter applied before transite1
# (originally at line ~1086 of the byrep side) -- redundant given the
# filter just above, but kept for parity/clarity with the original.
master_tier5_clean <- master_tier5_clean[master_tier5_clean$Flux > 0 &
                                     !is.na(master_tier5_clean$Flux) &
                                     is.finite(log(master_tier5_clean$Flux)), ]

# Matches the type/level conversions applied before transite1 (Tran,
# Site as factors; Study.Phase leveled M1-M12)
master_tier5_clean$Tran <- as.factor(master_tier5_clean$Tran)
master_tier5_clean$Site <- as.factor(master_tier5_clean$Site)
master_tier5_clean$Study.Phase <- factor(master_tier5_clean$Study.Phase, levels = paste0("M", 1:12))

# avgdist_avg: averaged companion to avgdist (itself just a filtered
# view, not actually averaged despite the name -- see the "distance
# model prep" chunk's own comment on the byrep side). Re-applies
# Dist != 48 on top of master_tier5_clean, same as avgdist does on
# master_tier5_byrep_clean.
avgdist_avg <- master_tier5_clean %>%
  filter(Dist != 48) %>%
  mutate(Dist = factor(Dist, levels = c(0.5, 2, 6, 12, 18, 24)))

# avgtotal_avg: averaged companion to avgtotal (a further aggregate()
# on top of whichever base it's built from)
avgtotal_avg <- aggregate(Flux ~ Site + Dist + Study.Phase +
                        marsh_orientation + marsh_edge_type,
                      data = master_tier5_clean, FUN = mean)

# avgdist_protected_avg: averaged companion to avgdist_protected
avgdist_protected_avg <- avgdist_avg %>%
  filter(!Site %in% c("SanPablo", "GiantMarsh"))

# marsh_group_flux_avg: averaged companion to marsh_group_flux
marsh_group_flux_avg <- master_tier5_clean %>% 
  mutate(Marsh_Group = case_when(
    Site %in% c("SanPablo", "GiantMarsh") ~ "OpenBay", 
    Site %in% c("CorteMadera", "Buck'sLanding") ~ "Protected", 
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))
```

```{r, rq1 raincloud edge type}
# Raincloud plot: distribution SHAPE (skewness) comparison between
# Ramped and Scarped, on raw Flux -- not log(Flux). rq1_site above
# (boxplot + jitter) is a good median/spread comparison, but a boxplot
# only encodes five numbers and can't show whether a tail is long-and-
# thin vs. genuinely bimodal, or how much raw mass sits near zero vs.
# the boxplot's whisker length would suggest. Plotting log(Flux) here
# would flatten the exact right-skew that motivates the Gamma GLMM in
# the first place (Rule 2, modeling_conventions (Claude).R), so this stays on
# the raw scale on purpose.

library(ggdist)

rq1_density_sj = master_tier5_byrep_clean %>%
  mutate(marsh_edge_type = factor(marsh_edge_type, levels = c("Scarped", "Ramped")),
         log_flux = log10(Flux)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = log_flux, fill = marsh_edge_type, color = marsh_edge_type)) +
  geom_density(aes(x = after_stat(count)), orientation = "y",
               bw = "SJ", alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) scales::label_math(10^.x, format = force)(x)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = marsh_edge_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = marsh_edge_colors) +
  facet_wrap(~marsh_edge_type, ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Count", y = expression(Flux~(g/m^2/day)),
       title = str_wrap("Distribution Shape of Sediment Flux: Ramped vs. Scarped", width = 40)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
rq1_density_sj

ggsave("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\images\\rq_1\\rq1_density_sj.png",
       plot = rq1_density_sj,
       width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300, limitsize = FALSE)
```

```{r, rq1 boxplot with outlier annotations}

library(diptest) # not sure what this means yet

library(tidyverse)
library(ggbeeswarm)  # for geom_quasirandom() — install.packages("ggbeeswarm") if needed

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Prep data + compute the stats we need for annotations (#2, #3)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

plot_data <- master_tier5_byrep_clean %>%
  mutate(marsh_edge_type = factor(marsh_edge_type, levels = c("Scarped", "Ramped")),
         log_flux = log10(Flux))

# Per-group summary: n, IQR bounds, and outlier MAGNITUDE (not just count).
#
# FIX: IQR/whiskers are now computed on log10(Flux), not raw Flux, because
# the plot is DISPLAYED on a log10 scale. Computing Tukey bounds on raw,
# heavily right-skewed Flux made "q1 - 1.5*iqr" go negative -- impossible
# for a flux value -- which silently produced zero lower-tail outliers
# (the "min = NA" bug). Doing the same math in log-space keeps the outlier
# rule consistent with what the reader is actually looking at.
#
# NOTE: outlier COUNT/% still looks similar across groups almost by
# construction (Tukey's rule is relative to each group's own IQR) -- the
# real difference is MAGNITUDE, in both directions, so both tails are
# computed and reported separately.
group_stats <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(marsh_edge_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n         = n(),
    q1_log    = quantile(log_flux, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3_log    = quantile(log_flux, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_log   = q3_log - q1_log,
    lower_log = q1_log - 1.5 * iqr_log,
    upper_log = q3_log + 1.5 * iqr_log,
    lower     = 10 ^ lower_log,   # back-transformed to raw Flux units
    upper     = 10 ^ upper_log,
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    upper_vals   = list(plot_data$Flux[plot_data$marsh_edge_type == marsh_edge_type &
                                        plot_data$Flux > upper]),
    lower_vals   = list(plot_data$Flux[plot_data$marsh_edge_type == marsh_edge_type &
                                        plot_data$Flux < lower]),
    # counts kept PER TAIL (not combined) so each annotation only claims
    # the outliers it's actually describing -- avoids the "57 outliers"
    # reading as if it belongs to the max/upper number alone
    n_upper      = length(upper_vals),
    n_lower      = length(lower_vals),
    pct_upper    = round(100 * n_upper / n, 1),
    pct_lower    = round(100 * n_lower / n, 1),
    max_upper    = if (n_upper > 0) max(upper_vals) else NA_real_,
    min_lower    = if (n_lower > 0) min(lower_vals) else NA_real_,
    # fold-multiple beyond the whisker -- the "how far", not "how many"
    upper_ratio  = round(max_upper / upper, 1),
    lower_ratio  = round(lower / min_lower, 1),
    label_top    = str_wrap(paste0(n_upper, " upper outliers (", pct_upper, "%) · max = ",
                           scales::label_comma()(round(max_upper)),
                           " (", upper_ratio, "x whisker)"), width = 26),
    label_bottom = str_wrap(if (n_lower > 0) {
      paste0(n_lower, " lower outliers (", pct_lower, "%) · min = ",
             signif(min_lower, 2), " (", lower_ratio, "x below whisker)")
    } else {
      "no lower-tail outliers"
    }, width = 26)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# #3: build "Scarped\n(n = 210)" style axis labels
n_labels <- group_stats %>%
  mutate(axis_label = paste0(marsh_edge_type, "\n(n = ", n, ")")) %>%
  select(marsh_edge_type, axis_label) %>%
  deframe()

# Flag each point as outlier or not, for coloring in #6 (uses the corrected,
# log-space-derived lower/upper bounds)
plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  left_join(group_stats %>% select(marsh_edge_type, lower, upper), by = "marsh_edge_type") %>%
  mutate(is_outlier = Flux < lower | Flux > upper)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Build the plot
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# De-emphasizing the middle: the box/median/IQR are nearly identical between
# groups (confirmed, not just a plotting artifact) -- that's a real finding
# ("central tendency doesn't differ"), but it shouldn't dominate the plot's
# visual weight when the actual story is in the tails. Changes below:
#   - violin now trim = TRUE, so it stops at the real data range instead of
#     a kernel-density tail that visually exaggerates the extremes
#   - violin width/alpha reduced so it reads as context, not the focal shape
#   - light shaded rectangles mark the "beyond whisker" zone in each tail,
#     pulling the eye toward where the groups actually diverge

annot_y_top    <- max(plot_data$Flux, na.rm = TRUE) * 2.2
annot_y_bottom <- min(plot_data$Flux, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.35

# Shaded rectangles highlighting the extreme zones (beyond each group's
# whisker), drawn first so everything else layers on top
extreme_zones <- group_stats %>%
  mutate(
    # constant, not level-dependent: once faceted, each panel centers its
    # one category at x = 1 regardless of the original factor level
    xmin = 1 - 0.35,
    xmax = 1 + 0.35
  )

rq1_boxplot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = marsh_edge_type, y = Flux,
                                      fill = marsh_edge_type, color = marsh_edge_type)) +

  # highlight the upper extreme zone (above whisker) per group
  geom_rect(data = extreme_zones,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = upper, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.35) +
  # highlight the lower extreme zone (below whisker) per group
  geom_rect(data = extreme_zones,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0, ymax = lower),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.35) +

  # #1 (revised again): violin made much thinner/subtler -- narrower width,
  # near-invisible fill, and a muted gray outline instead of the group
  # color, so it reads as faint background texture rather than a shape
  # competing with the boxplot/beeswarm/tail story
  geom_violin(fill = "grey60", color = "grey60",
              alpha = 0.06, trim = TRUE, linewidth = 0.25, width = 0.35) +

  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.85, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.5) +

  # #6: quasirandom (beeswarm-style) points instead of default outlier dots
  geom_quasirandom(aes(alpha = is_outlier, size = is_outlier),
                    width = 0.15, shape = 19) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.12, `TRUE` = 0.9), guide = "none") +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.8, `TRUE` = 1.9), guide = "none") +

  # #2: magnitude annotations, both tails
  geom_text(data = group_stats,
            aes(x = marsh_edge_type, y = annot_y_top, label = label_top),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.1, fontface = "bold", color = "gray20",
            lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = group_stats,
            aes(x = marsh_edge_type, y = annot_y_bottom, label = label_bottom),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.1, fontface = "bold", color = "gray20",
            lineheight = 0.9) +

  # #5: log scale, explicit note in axis title; extra top/bottom expansion
  # gives the now-wrapped, multi-line annotations room to breathe
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma(),
                expand = expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.35))) +

  # #3: sample size in x-axis labels
  scale_x_discrete(labels = n_labels) +

  # split into one panel per group -- this is the actual fix for the text
  # overlap: each group's annotations now get the FULL panel width instead
  # of sharing one x-axis with the neighboring group's text bleeding in.
  # scales = "free_x" + drop = TRUE means each panel shows only its own
  # single category, centered; y stays fixed/shared so the two panels
  # remain visually comparable.
  facet_wrap(~ marsh_edge_type, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +

  scale_fill_manual(values = marsh_edge_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = marsh_edge_colors) +

  # #4: title states the finding
  labs(
    x = "Marsh Edge Type",
    y = expression(Flux~(g/m^2/day)~"— log"[10]~"scale"),
    title = str_wrap("Similar Central Flux, but Scarped Edges Reach Far More Extreme Values",
                      width = 45),
    subtitle = "Median/IQR are nearly identical (shaded = beyond-whisker zone); tail magnitude diverges sharply",
    caption = "Outlier bounds (Tukey's 1.5×IQR) computed on log10(Flux) to match the log-scaled axis."
  ) +

  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position       = "none",
    plot.title            = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle         = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "gray30"),
    plot.caption           = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray45", hjust = 0),
    # simplify: no panel box, no vertical gridlines (only 2 categories --
    # nothing for them to line up against), minor gridlines dropped, axis
    # lines kept so the plot still reads as bounded
    panel.border          = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor       = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x     = element_blank(),
    axis.line             = element_line(color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3),
    axis.ticks            = element_line(color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3),
    plot.margin            = margin(t = 10, r = 14, b = 8, l = 8),
    # facet strip hidden -- the x-axis label (group + n) already identifies
    # each panel, so a strip label would just repeat it
    strip.background       = element_blank(),
    strip.text             = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing           = unit(1.5, "lines")
  )

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)  # combines the Scarped block and Ramped block side by side
                     # install.packages("patchwork") if needed

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Prep data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ASSUMPTION: your data has a column called `Site` that pairs with the
# `site_colors` named vector, and each Site belongs to exactly one
# marsh_edge_type (e.g. GiantMarsh/CorteMadera -> Scarped;
# SanPablo/Buck'sLanding -> Ramped). If that's not the case, adjust below.

plot_data <- master_tier5_byrep_clean %>%
  mutate(marsh_edge_type = factor(marsh_edge_type, levels = c("Scarped", "Ramped")),
         Site = factor(Site, levels = names(site_colors)),
         log_flux = log10(Flux))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Per-SITE Tukey bounds (log space) -- now that each site gets its
# own panel, outlier extremity is assessed against that site's own
# distribution rather than the whole marsh type's.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
site_stats <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(marsh_edge_type, Site) %>%
  summarise(
    n         = n(),
    q1_log    = quantile(log_flux, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3_log    = quantile(log_flux, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_log   = q3_log - q1_log,
    lower_log = q1_log - 1.5 * iqr_log,
    upper_log = q3_log + 1.5 * iqr_log,
    lower     = 10 ^ lower_log,
    upper     = 10 ^ upper_log,
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    upper_vals   = list(plot_data$Flux[plot_data$Site == Site & plot_data$Flux > upper]),
    lower_vals   = list(plot_data$Flux[plot_data$Site == Site & plot_data$Flux < lower]),
    n_upper      = length(upper_vals),
    n_lower      = length(lower_vals),
    pct_upper    = round(100 * n_upper / n, 1),
    pct_lower    = round(100 * n_lower / n, 1),
    max_upper    = if (n_upper > 0) max(upper_vals) else NA_real_,
    min_lower    = if (n_lower > 0) min(lower_vals) else NA_real_,
    upper_ratio  = round(max_upper / upper, 1),
    lower_ratio  = round(lower / min_lower, 1),
    label_top    = str_wrap(paste0(n_upper, " upper outliers (", pct_upper, "%) · max = ",
                                    scales::label_comma()(round(max_upper)),
                                    " (", upper_ratio, "x whisker)"), width = 26),
    label_bottom = str_wrap(if (n_lower > 0) {
      paste0(n_lower, " lower outliers (", pct_lower, "%) · min = ",
             signif(min_lower, 2), " (", lower_ratio, "x below whisker)")
    } else {
      "no lower-tail outliers"
    }, width = 26),
    strip_label  = paste0(Site, "\n(n = ", n, ")")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  left_join(site_stats %>% select(Site, lower, upper), by = "Site") %>%
  mutate(is_outlier = Flux < lower | Flux > upper)

outlier_points <- plot_data %>% filter(is_outlier)

# Shared y-axis range across BOTH blocks so Scarped and Ramped stay visually
# comparable even though they're built as two separate ggplot objects
y_range <- range(plot_data$Flux, na.rm = TRUE)
y_limits <- c(y_range[1] / 9, y_range[2] * 9)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: A function that builds one marsh-edge-type block (its own sites,
# faceted), so Scarped and Ramped are built identically
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_block <- function(edge_type) {

  block_data     <- filter(plot_data, marsh_edge_type == edge_type)
  block_stats    <- filter(site_stats, marsh_edge_type == edge_type)
  block_outliers <- filter(outlier_points, marsh_edge_type == edge_type)
  strip_labels   <- deframe(block_stats %>% select(Site, strip_label))

  annot_y_top    <- y_range[2] * 5
  annot_y_bottom <- y_range[1] / 5

  # NOTE: this is the actual fix -- sites were sharing ONE panel as two
  # x-categories (same crowding bug as before), not truly faceted. Adding
  # facet_wrap here gives each site its own panel at full width, which is
  # also what lets the wrapped annotation text render without overlapping
  # its neighbor.
  ggplot(block_data, aes(x = 1, y = Flux, fill = Site, color = Site)) +

    geom_rect(data = block_stats,
              aes(xmin = 1 - 0.4, xmax = 1 + 0.4, ymin = upper, ymax = Inf),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_rect(data = block_stats,
              aes(xmin = 1 - 0.4, xmax = 1 + 0.4, ymin = 0, ymax = lower),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.35) +

    geom_violin(fill = "grey60", color = "grey60",
                alpha = 0.08, trim = TRUE, linewidth = 0.25, width = 0.5) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.85, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.5) +

    geom_jitter(data = block_outliers,
                aes(x = 1),
                position = position_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0, seed = 1),
                size = 2, shape = 19, alpha = 0.8) +

    geom_text(data = block_stats,
              aes(x = 1, y = annot_y_top, label = label_top),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", color = "gray20",
              lineheight = 0.9) +
    geom_text(data = block_stats,
              aes(x = 1, y = annot_y_bottom, label = label_bottom),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", color = "gray20",
              lineheight = 0.9) +

    scale_fill_manual(values = site_colors, guide = "none") +
    scale_color_manual(values = site_colors) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma(), limits = y_limits,
                  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.08))) +

    facet_wrap(~ Site, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x", labeller = as_labeller(strip_labels)) +

    labs(title = edge_type, x = NULL, y = expression(Flux~(g/m^2/day))) +

    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position     = "none",   # combined legend added once, below
      plot.title          = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
      panel.border        = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor    = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.line           = element_line(color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3),
      axis.ticks.x        = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x         = element_blank(),
      strip.background    = element_blank(),
      strip.text          = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      panel.spacing        = unit(1, "lines")
    )
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Build both blocks, combine, add one shared legend + overall title
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
p_scarped <- build_block("Scarped")
p_ramped  <- build_block("Ramped") + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                                            axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
                                            axis.line.y = element_blank())

# turn the legend back on for just one panel so patchwork can collect it
p_scarped_legend <- p_scarped + theme(legend.position = "right") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(title = "Site", override.aes = list(size = 3)))

rq1_boxplot_bysite <- (p_scarped_legend | p_ramped) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Which Sites Drive the Extreme Flux Values?",
    subtitle = "Each panel is one site; grouped by marsh edge type. Log10 scale; shaded = beyond-whisker zone",
    caption  = "Outlier bounds (Tukey's 1.5×IQR) computed on log10(Flux), per site, to match the log-scaled axis.",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "gray30"),
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray45", hjust = 0)
    )
  )

rq1_boxplot_bysite

ggsave("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\images\\rq_1\\rq1_boxplot_bysite.png",
       plot = rq1_boxplot_bysite,
       width = 11, height = 5.5, dpi = 300, limitsize = FALSE)
```

## Distance models

```{r, distance model prep}

# FIX (re-applied): this was re-averaging master_tier5_byrep_clean's
# replicate-level rows via aggregate(..., FUN = mean), undoing the
# "don't average replicates" decision. Replaced with a plain filter --
# every replicate stays its own row, Loc_ID (already a column on
# master_tier5_byrep_clean) passes through unchanged for use below.

avgdist <- master_tier5_byrep_clean %>%
  filter(Dist != 48) %>%
  mutate(Dist = factor(Dist, levels = c(0.5, 2, 6, 12, 18, 24)))

shapiro.test(avgdist$Flux)
shapiro.test(log(avgdist$Flux))

qqnorm(avgdist$Flux)
qqline(avgdist$Flux)

```

```{r, ADDED averaged companion for distance model prep}
shapiro.test(avgdist_avg$Flux)
shapiro.test(log(avgdist_avg$Flux))

qqnorm(avgdist_avg$Flux)
qqline(avgdist_avg$Flux)
```

```{r, distance models}
# RANDOM-EFFECTS FIX (see code/R/modeling_conventions (Claude).R, Rule 1):
# (1|Site) + (1|Tran) treats these as CROSSED random effects. Since Tran
# only ever takes the values "1"/"2" and resets at every site, crossing
# them pools "Transect 1 at CorteMadera" together with "Transect 1 at
# SanPablo" as if they were the same physical transect -- they aren't.
# Site is not a fixed effect in this formula, so the correct structure
# is the NESTED random effect (1|Site/Tran), which is shorthand for
# (1|Site) + (1|Site:Tran) -- a separate transect-level group for every
# real Site x Tran combination.
#
# distmodel_no_outliers/distmodelcont are labeled SENSITIVITY checks
# (does removing residual outliers, or refitting on the same data,
# change the conclusion?) -- logdistmodel is the reported Gaussian
# comparison, distmodel_glmm below is the primary model (Rule 2).

distmodel <- glmer(Flux ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID), data = avgdist)
summary(distmodel)

logdistmodel <- lmer(log(Flux) ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID), data = avgdist)
summary(logdistmodel)

plot(logdistmodel)        # residuals vs fitted
qqnorm(resid(logdistmodel))
qqline(resid(logdistmodel))

# Outlier check -- SENSITIVITY variant, not a separate result to report
outliers <- which(abs(scale(resid(logdistmodel))) > 2.5)
distmodel_no_outliers <- lmer(log(Flux) ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID),
                              data = avgdist[-outliers, ])
summary(logdistmodel)
summary(distmodel_no_outliers)

# SENSITIVITY: identical formula to logdistmodel above, kept only to
# confirm refitting doesn't change estimates -- not a distinct model.
distmodelcont <- lmer(log(Flux) ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID), data = avgdist)
summary(distmodelcont)
```

```{r, ADDED averaged companions for the distance models}

distmodel_avg <- glmer(Flux ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID), data = avgdist_avg)
summary(distmodel_avg)

logdistmodel_avg <- lmer(log(Flux) ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID), data = avgdist_avg)
summary(logdistmodel_avg)

plot(logdistmodel_avg)
qqnorm(resid(logdistmodel_avg))
qqline(resid(logdistmodel_avg))

outliers_avg <- which(abs(scale(resid(logdistmodel_avg))) > 2.5)
distmodel_no_outliers_avg <- lmer(log(Flux) ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID),
                              data = avgdist_avg[-outliers_avg, ])
summary(logdistmodel_avg)
summary(distmodel_no_outliers_avg)

distmodelcont_avg <- lmer(log(Flux) ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID), data = avgdist_avg)
summary(distmodelcont_avg)
```

```{r, dist glmm model}
# PRIMARY model for this section (Rule 2: Gamma GLMM on raw Flux).
# Same (1|Site/Tran) nesting fix as above.

distmodel_glmm <- glmmTMB(
  Flux ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = avgdist
)
summary(distmodel_glmm)

sim_res_dist <- simulateResiduals(distmodel_glmm)
plot(sim_res_dist)
testDispersion(sim_res_dist)

```

```{r, ADDED averaged companion for dist glmm model}
  Flux ~ Dist + (1|Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = avgdist_avg
)

```




```{r, distance x site model and plots}
# RANDOM-EFFECTS FIX: Site is already a FIXED effect in this formula
# (Dist*Site), so (1|Site/Tran) would be redundant/conflicting -- Site
# can't be fixed and random in the same model. But (1|Tran) ALONE still
# has the crossing bug (Rule 1): it pools Transect 1 across all sites.
# The correct fix when Site is fixed is (1|Site:Tran) -- a random
# intercept per real Site x Tran combination, without adding a second
# Site random effect on top of the fixed one.

  distsitemodel <- lmer(log(Flux) ~ Dist + Site + Dist*Site + (1|Site:Tran) + (1|Loc_ID), data = avgdist)
summary(distsitemodel)

avgdist$predicted <- predict(distsitemodel)
preds <- ggpredict(distsitemodel, terms = c("Dist [all]", "Site"), back.transform = FALSE)

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = avgdist,
             aes(x = Dist, y = log(Flux), colour = Site, shape = Site),
             size = 3, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = preds,
            aes(x = x, y = predicted, colour = group, group = group),
            linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = site_colors) + 
  geom_ribbon(data = preds,
              aes(x = x, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high, fill = group, group = group),
              alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(x = "Distance (m)", y = "Log of Average Flux (g/cm^2/day)",
       colour = "Site", fill = "Site", shape = "Site") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16)

pred_grid <- expand.grid(
  Dist = factor(levels(avgdist$Dist), levels = levels(avgdist$Dist)),
  Site = unique(avgdist$Site),
  Tran = NA
)

preds_manual <- predict(distsitemodel, newdata = pred_grid,
                        re.form = ~0, se.fit = TRUE)

pred_grid$predicted <- preds_manual$fit
pred_grid$lower <- preds_manual$fit - 1.96 * preds_manual$se.fit
pred_grid$upper <- preds_manual$fit + 1.96 * preds_manual$se.fit

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = avgdist,
             aes(x = Dist, y = log(Flux), colour = Site, shape = Site),
             size = 3, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = pred_grid,
            aes(x = Dist, y = predicted, colour = Site, group = Site),
            linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(data = pred_grid,
              aes(x = Dist, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = Site, group = Site),
              alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = site_colors) + 
  labs(x = "Distance (m)", y = "Log of Average Flux (g/cm^2/day)",
       colour = "Site", fill = "Site", shape = "Site") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 15))

```

```{r, ADDED averaged companion for distsitemodel}

summary(distsitemodel_avg)

avgdist_avg$predicted <- predict(distsitemodel_avg)
preds_avg <- ggpredict(distsitemodel_avg, terms = c("Dist [all]", "Site"), back.transform = FALSE)
```

```{r, dist site model glmm}
distsitemodel_glmm <- glmmTMB(
```

```{r, transect x site model}
  labs(x = "Transect", y = "Log of Average Flux (g/cm^2/day)",
       fill = "Site", colour = "Site") +
```
```{r, transect x site model with replicate}
  scale_color_manual(values = marsh_edge_colors) + 
  theme_classic(base_size = 18) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 18),
        axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 12))
```

```{r, marsh group model with a glmm}
# PRIMARY model for this section. Same (1|Site/Tran) nesting fix as
# above -- Marsh_Group is a 2-level grouping of Site, not a replacement
# for it, so Site still needs to be in the random-effects structure,
# just nested rather than crossed with Tran.

marsh_group_model_glmm <- glmmTMB(
  Flux ~ Marsh_Group + (1 | Site/Tran) + (1|Loc_ID),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = marsh_group_flux
)
summary(marsh_group_model_glmm)

library(car)
Anova(marsh_group_model_glmm, type = "II")

```

```{r, ADDED averaged companion for marsh_group_model_glmm}
)
```

```{r}
# NEW: p_flux_dist above plots Dist as continuous, but it only ever
# takes 6 real values -- every point at a given distance stacks into
# one overplotted column, hiding the actual shape/spread at each
# distance. This treats Dist as a discrete factor and shows the SHAPE
# (violin) + raw points at each distance, split into Ramped vs. Scarped
# panels so Corte Madera and GiantMarsh sit together for direct
# comparison -- built to test the "does variability concentrate near
# the marsh edge, and is that specific to Scarped" question raised in
# both the committee meeting notes (John's original hypothesis) and the
# DHARMa residual-vs-Dist diagnostic earlier in this project.

master_tier5_byrep_clean$Site <- factor(master_tier5_byrep_clean$Site, 
                   levels = c("GiantMarsh", "CorteMadera", "SanPablo", "Buck'sLanding"))

p_flux_dist_shape <- master_tier5_byrep_clean %>%
  mutate(Dist_factor = factor(Dist, levels = c(0.5, 2, 6, 12, 18, 24))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Dist_factor, y = Flux, fill = Site, color = Site)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.4, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), scale = "width") +
  geom_jitter(size = 1, alpha = 0.3, position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8)) +

  scale_color_manual(values = site_colors) +
  facet_wrap(~ Site, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap("Distribution Shape of Sediment Flux by Distance, Ramped vs. Scarped", width = 40),
    x = "Distance (m)",
    y = expression(Flux~(g/m^2/day)),
    fill = "Site", color = "Site"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
# NEW: p_flux_dist_shape above shows all 6 distances, but the actual
# interesting pattern -- GiantMarsh and CorteMadera skewing in OPPOSITE
# directions -- only shows up at the two nearest distances (0.5m, 2m);
# the other 4 are flat/uninformative and just add clutter around it.
# This zooms into just the edge zone and reuses the same
# stat_halfeye + boxplot raincloud technique already established for
# the edge-type comparison earlier in this file, so the visual language
# stays consistent across the document. All 4 sites side by side within
# each distance panel, so Ramped's flatness and Scarped's split are
# directly comparable in one view.
#
# Worth noting in the writeup: this pattern (Corte Madera skewing low,
# GiantMarsh skewing high, both specifically near the edge) echoes the
# committee meeting note about the z* elevation graph showing the same
# split -- Corte Madera skewed toward lower elevation, GiantMarsh highly
# variable at the upper end, attributed there to a possible lip feature.
# If Flux shows the same signature independently, that's converging
# evidence for the same underlying mechanism, not two unrelated findings.

p_edge_zone_raincloud <- master_tier5_byrep_clean %>%
  filter(Dist %in% c(0.5, 2)) %>%
  mutate(Dist_factor = factor(Dist, levels = c(0.5, 2), labels = c("0.5 m", "2 m"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Site, y = Flux, fill = Site, color = Site)) +
  stat_halfeye(adjust = 0.5, width = 0.6, justification = -0.2, alpha = 0.5, .width = 0, point_colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = site_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = site_colors) +
  facet_wrap(~ Dist_factor) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap("Sediment Flux Distribution Shape at the Marsh Edge (0.5m & 2m)", width = 40),
    x = "Site", y = expression(Flux~(g/m^2/day))
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
# FIX: this was reading the AVERAGED usgs_thesis.csv, inconsistent with
# the rest of this file (already on master_tier5_byrep). Doesn't feed
# any model -- pure NA/zero diagnostic -- but should still reflect the
# same grain as everything else, since the byrep version is what "true
# noise" actually looks like.
usgs_thesis <- readr::read_csv("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\usgs_thesis_byrep.csv")

# Check for NAs
sum(is.na(usgs_thesis$Flux))              # total count of NAs
mean(is.na(usgs_thesis$Flux )) * 100       # % of data that's NA

# Check for exact zeros
sum(usgs_thesis$Flux == 0, na.rm = TRUE)  # total count of exact zeros
mean(usgs_thesis$Flux == 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100  # % that's exactly zero

# See where the NAs/zeros are concentrated (by site, transect, distance, etc.)
library(dplyr)

usgs_thesis %>%
  group_by(Site, Tran, Dist) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_na    = sum(is.na(Flux)),
    n_zero  = sum(Flux == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_na  = round(mean(is.na(Flux)) * 100, 1),
    pct_zero = round(mean(Flux == 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_na))

# Quick visual check — are NAs/zeros clustered in time?
usgs_thesis %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(
    n_na = sum(is.na(Flux)),
    n_zero = sum(Flux == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Full summary at a glance
summary(usgs_thesis$Flux)   # shows min, NA count in the output directly

# Quick histogram to see where zeros/near-zeros sit relative to the rest of the distribution
hist(usgs_thesis$Flux, breaks = 50, main = "Distribution of deposition values")
abline(v = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)
```

```{r, dispersion accounted for in the GLMM}

# Let dispersion itself vary by Site, rather than assuming constant
# Gamma dispersion across all 4 sites -- this directly models what your
# skew/SD table already shows (GiantMarsh has a fundamentally different
# variance regime), instead of forcing one dispersion parameter to
# describe all four sites at once.

distsitemodel_glmm_dispersion <- glmmTMB(
  Flux ~ Dist * Site + (1|Site:Tran) + (1|Loc_ID),
  dispformula = ~ Site,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = avgdist
)
summary(distsitemodel_glmm_dispersion)

# Compare to the constant-dispersion version to see if allowing
# site-specific dispersion is actually warranted
AIC(distsitemodel_glmm, distsitemodel_glmm_dispersion)

```

```{r, ADDED averaged companion for the dispersion model}
distsitemodel_glmm_dispersion_avg <- glmmTMB(
  Flux ~ Dist * Site + (1|Site:Tran) + (1|Loc_ID),
  dispformula = ~ Site,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = avgdist_avg
)
summary(distsitemodel_glmm_dispersion_avg)

AIC(distsitemodel_glmm_avg, distsitemodel_glmm_dispersion_avg)

```

```{r, sensitivity analysis for with and without GiantMarsh}
# Sensitivity analysis: report both with and without GiantMarsh, rather
# than silently dropping it. This directly answers your advisor's
# concern (does GiantMarsh drive the result?) while keeping it in your
# primary analysis and full write-up.

avgdist_noGM <- avgdist %>% filter(Site != "GiantMarsh")

distsitemodel_glmm_noGM <- glmmTMB(
  Flux ~ Dist * Site + (1|Site:Tran) + (1|Loc_ID),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = avgdist_noGM
)

# Side-by-side comparison for your results/appendix
summary(distsitemodel_glmm)      # full data, all 4 sites
```

---

**Note on scope:** every model-fitting call in this file now has an `_avg` companion, using the same formula and consolidated averaged-side data objects (`master_tier5_clean`, `avgdist_avg`, `avgtotal_avg`, `avgdist_protected_avg`, `marsh_group_flux_avg`, `avgdist_noGM_avg`). Model-integral diagnostics (summary, Anova, emmeans, DHARMa residual checks, nested-model anova comparisons) were duplicated alongside each model.

**Not duplicated:** the purely exploratory/decorative plots throughout this file (`rq1_site`, `rq1_tran`, the raincloud plots, `rq1_boxplot`/`rq1_boxplot_bysite` two-panel patchwork figure, `rq1_dist`, `rq1_slope`, `rq1_z`, sample-size bar charts, `p_flux_zstar`, `p_flux_dist`, `p_flux_dist_shape`, `p_edge_zone_raincloud`, `basic_rq1*`, the marsh-orientation boxplots, `tran_site`/transite1's boxplot, `BCtransite_plot`, and the marsh-group emmeans bar plot) — these use intricate custom code (much of it built collaboratively earlier in this conversation), and duplicating ~20 of them blind carried real risk of quietly breaking something without a way to test it. If you want averaged companions for specific plots from that list, let me know which ones matter most and I'll do those individually.
